body: **2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap** — measured the obs log format for escher's own sink: one text line per event on stderr behind the allowlist scrub, printing only `node_id` / `status` / `waiting_nodes` / `property` / `log.*` for `blitz*` and `accesskit_xplat` targets and redacting `text`, `value`, `html`, `attrs`. This is the scrub by field name in `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` that the chunk reuses on every `caused` record. A record from an engine target crosses with its safe fields alone, so the chunk's rule (a hidden field shown by name with the marker, the rest of the message still crossing) has to be settled against this one.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — added the sink's third outcome: a record from any target outside `blitz*`, `accesskit_xplat` and `escher_*` is dropped whole at every level, and `escher_*` targets redact the four content fields. The chunk wants app, framework and engine records with their target and fields in the answer. The answer must widen what it captures without moving this drop on the log sink's own lines, which the scope's boundary keeps unchanged. A future a11y violation record also reaches the log only under an engine or `escher_` target.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — restated the sink as two record classes: event lines, and one line per closed span of an admitted target, every pair judged by the same allowlist. It also added `tracing` as escher-driver's third dependency, with no feature. The scope keeps the `command` and `tool_call` spans' fixed fields, and error text must reach no span field. This entry is where that span class and its scrub are stated.

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** — the sink's second record class (closed-span lines) now reads ratified by the founder in §3's note. The span line format the chunk must leave untouched is ratified, not provisional.

**2026-10-06-snapshot-state-fidelity** — the snapshot reads `value` from the element, and a password input reads `MASKED_VALUE` (contract/snapshot/password-value). The scope says the ratified mask is unmoved and a password's value never crosses. Error, log or panic text carrying a typed password (for example an `Err` that quotes the input's value) must not bypass this mask through `caused`.

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — extended the mask to a file input: it reads the marker where its `value` is non-empty, its path in no snapshot field (contract/snapshot/file-input-value). It also put `Snapshot::to_text` under the `accessibility` feature as a reader of the model. A file path that turns up in an error message or log field is the same secret, and the chunk's scrub must keep it out of the answer.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — measured a password typed through MCP `type` reading `MASKED_VALUE` in the tool result, the sentinel 0 times, in both layout modes. It also added the node keys' help as a reader of the snapshot model, closed words only. This is the precedent for the chunk's MCP acceptance (a sentinel count of 0 over the whole result) and for `describe()`'s help naming new fields in closed words.

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — a password's text is in no painted frame either (decision/password-never-revealed, ratified fork 2). The screenshot is one more reader of the model's bounds and changes nothing. This completes the "never revealed" rule that the error text must not break on any carrier.

**2026-10-19-shared-fixtures** — the MCP masked-password input moved to the shared page `fixtures::password_named` in `tests/blitz-tests/tests/fixtures/mod.rs`. This is the ready fixture for the chunk's acceptance that a password value never crosses in `caused`.

**2026-10-06-accessibility-tree-identity** — the workspace takes the Dioxus crates with `default-features = false`, so a crate gets `accessibility` only by naming it (decision/dioxus-accessibility-feature-by-name). dioxus-native-dom's feature gates its tree override. If the chunk reads boundary errors in `packages/dioxus-native-dom/src/boundary.rs`, it must decide whether that reading is gated, and this entry is where the feature wiring is set.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — at that point escher-driver named no dioxus-native-dom feature, and the entry that first read the snapshot through a session was to decide the feature. This is the starting state that act-by-id later reversed.

**2026-10-07-act-by-id** — escher-driver now names `accessibility` on dioxus-native-dom unconditionally, with no `[features]` table of its own, so the feature reaches both seven_guis binaries (decision/driver-requires-accessibility). No platform adapter is built, and the lockfile was byte-identical. The chunk's new `caused` text in `packages/escher-driver/src/caused.rs` runs under this always-on feature. Any new dependency must be re-read against the stand graph's adapter probe (`accesskit_(xplat|winit)` 0 rows).

**2026-10-06-snapshot-model** — `DioxusDocument::snapshot` takes role, name and focus from the accessibility tree, with no second role or name mapping (decision/snapshot-model-single-source). The chunk's text joins acting answers beside the diff. It must add no role or name reading of its own, only error and log text.

**2026-10-07-change-tracking-and-diff** — `Snapshot::diff` is one more reader of the snapshot model, also gated by `accessibility`. An acting call's answer carries this diff (contract/mcp-result/snapshot). The `caused` text rides the same JSON line, beside the diff and apart from it.

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — an MCP tool result reads the snapshot model and nothing else: a `snapshot` result is `to_text`'s output, and an acting call's is its JSON line with the diff (contract/mcp-result/snapshot). It also added escher-driver's `serde_json` dependency and re-read the stand graph. The chunk widens that acting JSON line with error text on the ratified MCP crossing. The contract row has to state the addition, and the 1,048,576-byte bound holds over it.

**2026-10-20-large-screen-in-parts** — `Snapshot::text_parts` is a further reader under `accessibility`, and an MCP `snapshot` result is the JSON line `{text, part, parts}` for a paged screen. A password reads `MASKED_VALUE` in every part. This is the precedent for bounding an answer by a budget, and the MCP contract row the chunk's carrier change sits beside.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (how an open list's labels leave) — ratified that an option's label and a group's `label` leave an open list only as painted pixels and the snapshot's `name`, with no log site (decision/option-labels-leave-only-as-pixels). The chunk carries log records and their fields into the answer. It must not open a new route for page-authored labels through a captured log record or message.

**2026-10-31-engine-debts** (the driver on a `multiple` select) — `type` on a `multiple` select focuses it with no click, adding no verb, argument, key name, result field, cause, session error or exit to the driver's closed sets (decision/driver-type-focuses-select-no-click). The chunk adds result fields under `caused`. This row's list of closed sets is where that addition has to be squared, and the scope's boundary of no new verb, cause, session error or exit matches it.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** (the driver's `type` on any select) — widened the `type` row to any select (`focus_select`, which also closes any list), still with no closed-set addition. This is the current form of the row named in item 18.

**2026-11-07-ui-graph** (the read-only UI graph reader) — put `DioxusDocument::graph` behind `accessibility`, with the `signal_registry` module not gated (decision/agent-readers-behind-accessibility). It answers names and closed words only, never a value. This is the gating line and the "never a value" precedent the chunk's text in `caused` breaks on purpose, inside the founder's answer.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the actionable-node reader) — added `actionable_nodes` to the gated set, sharing the crate-private actionable rule with `unkeyed_actionable`. The gated readers' list is extended here; any reader the chunk adds to dioxus-native-dom (such as the boundary error's message) belongs on this list or beside the ungated ones.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the actions verb as a read-only reader) — the `actions` answer writes ids, owner ids, verb and cause words and booleans only, never a value, typed text, `MASKED_VALUE` or `NodeId`, measured with a typed sentinel. This is the precedent for a sentinel acceptance on a driver answer. The chunk's `caused` text is the first answer field to carry free text beyond that rule.

**2026-11-08-what-can-i-do-here** (the one actionable rule) — `unkeyed_actionable` and `actionable_nodes` read one rule, with the listener leg the vdom walk's exact current listeners (decision/actionable-key rule, guard `unkeyed_actionable`). This is relevant if the chunk's fixtures add failing handlers: each actionable element must carry an author key or the guard reports it.

**2026-10-06-id-stability-across-code-edits** — set the actionable-key rule (founder) and its check `unkeyed_actionable`. Trap: never satisfy the check by adding a `tabindex` or a role; key the element. This applies to any button the chunk adds to a fixture or stand page to raise a panic or `Err`.

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** (the ungated reached record) — dioxus-native-dom's `reached` module (`ReachedHandler`, `record_reached`, `reached_handlers`, crate-private `element_listener_ids`) is ungated, written on `handle_event`'s path before `runtime.handle_event`, because the wasm build compiles dioxus-native-dom without `accessibility`. `caused`, built by 2026-11-16-errors-with-the-action by handler, rests on this record. Any new boundary or error reading on that path must likewise compile without the feature.

**2026-11-12T03-36-23-rows** — turned the master's text into rows (241), each verified against the code. The picked rows (driver-requires-accessibility, agent-readers-behind-accessibility, password-value-masked, contract/mcp-result/snapshot and the rest) took their current wording here. Any `~ {handle}` change this chunk owes, such as the MCP acting-result contract gaining error text, edits these rows.

An acting answer's caused (click, type, press, advance, scroll) gains, per record, the text of what the step caused: a panic's payload and source location, an error's message and its whole cause chain, a log record's message, target, level, location and fields from the app, the UI framework and the engine.
Every field passes the log sink's existing scrub by field name; a hidden field shows its name and the redaction marker and the rest of the message still crosses; the password and file input mask stays unmoved.
Each message is cut at a fixed length and an answer carries a fixed count of records, both set from measured real message lengths; a cut says it was cut and by how much, and records past the count are counted by source.
The text rides every carrier caused rides today (in-process Outcome, command line JSON line, session socket call, MCP tool result, kept check) inside the MCP and socket answer bounds, and describe() names the new fields.
Research first measures message lengths on the stand and fixtures and whether an app's own error boundary can be read; an unread boundary is said by the tool's help.

body: The acting answer's caused field on every acting verb (click, type, press, advance, scroll) gains per-record text: message, source location, cause chain, target, level and fields.
A panic's payload and its source location (file, line, column) cross into the answer as the panic hook reads them.
An error the app's root error boundary took crosses with its message and every source in its cause chain, not its top line alone.
Log records from the app, the UI framework and the engine cross with message, target, level, bridged log location and fields; engine and escher targets are now admitted to the answer's capture.

Every field of every crossing record passes the existing scrub by field name: the content field names stay redacted, the engine's safe-field rule holds, a hidden field shows its name and the redaction marker and the rest of the message still crosses.
The ratified value mask is unmoved: a password input's value and a file input's value never cross in an answer, through error text or otherwise.

The log sink's own lines are unchanged: the printed event and closed span line formats, the target allowlist and its per-target field rules, and the command and tool_call spans' fixed fields; no message, payload or field value reaches a log line or span field that does not already.

The cut and the count are measured values: each message cut at a fixed length, a fixed count of records per answer, set from measured lengths on the stand and fixtures; a cut message states it was cut and by how much, and records past the count are counted by source.
Research measures real message lengths on the stand's tasks and the fixtures (a panic with location, an error with source chain, engine and framework records) before the bound is set.
Research measures whether an error an app's own error boundary component catches can be read by the driver at all, and with what; what is not read is stated by the tool's own help, never silent.

The text rides every carrier caused rides: the in-process Outcome, the command line's JSON line, the session socket's call, an MCP tool result and a kept check recorded, replayed and kept whole; the MCP result bound of 1,048,576 bytes and the socket answer bound hold over it.
describe()'s self-description names caused's new fields and the meaning of the cut and the count.
No new verb, carrier, exit, refusal cause, session error, socket or listener; the actions answer and the driver refusal causes stay as they are.

Acceptance: a fixture with a real failure (a panic in a real code path, an Err with a cause chain, a framework or engine record) whose answer alone asserts the message, the source location and the cause chain, not only the fields' presence.
Acceptance: a record with a secret-named field crosses with that field hidden and the rest whole; a message past the cut arrives cut with the cut said; records past the count are counted by source.
Acceptance runs in both layout modes, in process, through the command line and over MCP.
The session library always enables accessibility, so the acting verbs and their answers are built with the accessibility feature on.

new checks are Rust tests run in the tier and leg their kind belongs to, gating CI

ARIA patterns and roles, hidden content and native element roles: the chunk changes nothing of what the tree holds or hides.
Keyboard navigation, focus, select lists, range inputs and keyboard activation contracts: the chunk changes no input behaviour, only what an acting answer reports a step caused.

Accessibility scope and platform reach: the accessibility tier, the platform adapter, AccessKit as the tree and browser feature defaults are not changed.

**2026-11-16-errors-with-the-action** — (Standard Contracts: 6 rows) added `contract/acting-verb-results/caused` (closed words, ids and counts only), `decision/capture-dispatcher-pair`, `contract/reached-record/take-step-reached` and `contract/dioxus-native-dom-api/root-error-mark` (`RootErrorMark` compares by identity, its Debug prints its name alone), and changed `contract/answer-json/outcome` (caused only when non-empty) and `contract/busy-classes/render`. This is the register this chunk extends: `caused` gains text, `RootErrorMark` must start reading the error and its source chain, and the dispatcher-pair design (its rejected per-thread alternative) constrains how the capture can admit more targets.

**2026-11-16-errors-with-the-action** — (Conventions; Established Decisions; Cross-cutting Patterns; Standard Contracts) added `decision/capture-before-own-recorder` (an operator CI fix: a stand check that installs its own recorder opens an empty capture first). Narrowed `decision/driver-library-side-effect-free`, `decision/driver-spans-only` and `decision/escher-driver-spans-ungated` to "no global subscriber", with only escher-telemetry's scoped capture default around an acting step. Added `boundary` to the ungated modules of `decision/accessibility-feature-gating`, and reworded `contract/telemetry/target-filter` so the drop is the sink's alone, since the capture counts outside targets. Widening the capture to engine and escher targets and to their text extends each of these rows. The sink's drop and scrub rules must stay the sink's.

**2026-10-06-telemetry-bootstrap** — registered escher-telemetry: `init`, the stderr line shape, the allowlist scrub and the panic event (target `escher_telemetry::panic`, `panic.file` / `line` / `column`, a redacted `panic.payload`, then the previous hook). This is the origin of `contract/telemetry-panic/panic-event` and `contract/telemetry/panic-hook`. The chunk reads the panic's payload and location from the same hook, and the payload is redacted on the log line, so carrying it in the answer must not change what the sink prints.

**2026-10-07-sink-target-allowlist** — set the two public prefix sets `ENGINE_TARGET_PREFIXES` and `ESCHER_TARGET_PREFIXES`. An engine target prints only `SAFE_FIELDS`, an escher target prints every field but `CONTENT_FIELDS`, and any other target is dropped whole at every level, with the drop in the formatter. These are the scrub-by-field-name rules in `packages/escher-telemetry/src/format.rs` that the chunk reuses for answer text, and the origin of the telemetry-scrub rows. The standing rule: a third-party record never reaches the sink, and the chunk's widened capture must not change that.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — (the command span; `tracing` the third dependency) set the `command` span's eight fields, recorded only where they apply. It is never fielded with screen text, label, ids, arguments, `Outcome` or `Refusal`, and is built by hand with no `#[instrument]`. Its PROVISIONAL sibling entry added the sink's closed-span line, judged by the event rule. The chunk's boundary keeps these fixed fields: the error text crosses only as the answer, never as a span field (`contract/command-span/never-fielded`, `decision/driver-hand-built-spans`).

**2026-10-09-founder-rulings** — ratified the closed-span line and the rule that a diff's counts may reach a log while its content never may. This is the precedent the chunk's "no message, payload or field value reaches a log line" boundary follows: counts in logs are allowed, content is not.

**2026-10-07-driver-session** — (driver session registered) added escher-driver, the Unix socket and the `escher-session` host, and a second `escher_telemetry::init` install site. It set the standing rule that the first request carrying screen content is a new crossing question, and returns Unsupported off unix. This is the origin of `decision/session-over-unix-socket`, `decision/cross-process-session-unsupported-on-windows` and `decision/telemetry-one-install-site`.

**2026-10-10-driver-cli** — (the socket carries a call and its answer) made the socket carry ids, names, masked values, snapshot text and diffs out, a ratified widening, and stated that no log carries any of it. Its contract sibling set the 1,048,576-byte answer bound, the `oversize` reply and `AnswerTooLarge`, and the hand-written JSON forms. Error text is new page- and app-authored content on this carrier, and must fit the same bound (`contract/session-wire/ok-oversize`, `contract/session-errors/answer-too-large`).

**2026-10-10-mcp-surface** — added the MCP server over the `mcp` role's stdio (a ratified crossing; the next surface carrying screen content asks again), with the result bound of 1,048,576 bytes. It took `serde_json` as a reader only and added the `tool_call` span with `tool` and `ending` only. Standing rule: no span field holds what a call supplied or a screen reads. The chunk's text rides the MCP tool result under that bound and adds no span field.

**2026-10-12-self-description** — added `help` / `describe()` from the tables, and ratified that the program's own fixed `'static` text rides the carriers. "Text from a page, a call or a screen, a new carrier or a new exit still widens." This is the trap for this chunk: `describe()` naming the new `caused` fields is fixed text inside the ratified carriers, while the error text itself is page- and app-authored content, a widening owed its ratification (`decision/fixed-program-text-on-carriers`).

**2026-10-12-headless-screenshot** — sent a shot's pixels in band (ratified) and bounded an MCP result holding an image by its whole written form (`ToolResult::bounded`), with the bounds unchanged. This is the precedent for a larger answer under the same 1,048,576-byte bound: a `screenshot` step's `caused` text adds to that bound (`decision/screenshot-in-band`, `contract/mcp-server/result-bound`).

**2026-10-06-compact-snapshot-serialization** — extended the snapshot `value` mask to a password and a file input: `MASKED_VALUE`, never the text, its length or a host path. Later the mask applied on every carrier and in kept checks (`decision/masked-input-values`, `contract/node-keys/value`). The scope keeps the mask unmoved, and error and log text must not reintroduce a masked value or a file path through a message.

This is the origin of `decision/recorded-session-checks`, `decision/recorded-session-kept-check` and `decision/kept-check-never-logged`. A `caused` with text is kept at rest in every recorded acting step.

The committed checks must stay free of host paths (`contract/check-replay/first-difference`, `decision/committed-stand-checks`).

**2026-10-20-load-wait** — added the acting step's bounded load wait (`settle_waiting`, `LOAD_WAIT` 5 s). It reads `Instant` and sleeps only, with no time move, no print and no `tracing` call. This is the origin of the load-wait rows. The capture that `caused` is read from wraps this step, so new text capture must keep the wait's "no tracing call" and "no time moves" promises (`contract/load-wait/no-time-moves`).

This is the origin of `decision/refusal-causes-closed-at-eight` and `decision/advance-moves-session-clock`. The root error boundary's taken error read for its message and cause chain, where today it is held by identity and read for nothing.

The log capture behind caused admits the app's, the UI framework's and the engine's records, engine and escher targets included, while the log sink's own target allowlist and the lines it writes stay as they are.

The scrub by field name over every field of every record in caused: a field the content field names or the safe-field rule hide is shown by its name and the redaction marker, and the rest of the message still crosses, never blanked whole.
The ratified mask is unmoved: a typed password's or a file input's value never crosses in caused text, on any carrier.
The message cut: each message cut at a fixed length set from the measured lengths, a cut message saying it was cut and by how much; never a silent cut.
The record count: an answer holds at most a fixed count of records, set from measurement, the records past it counted by source.

Research measures real message lengths on the stand and fixtures, a panic with its location, an error with its source chain, the engine's and the framework's records a stand task's acting step causes, before the cut and the count are fixed.
Research reads whether an error an app's own error boundary, not the root one, catches can be read by the driver, and with what; an unread boundary is said in the tool's own help, never silent.

The carriers of caused: the in-process Outcome, the command line's JSON line, the session socket's call answer, the MCP tool result, and a kept check recorded and replayed with its answer kept whole, all carrying the same text.
The answer bounds hold over the new text: the MCP tool result bound of 1,048,576 bytes and the session wire's answer bound, an oversize answer staying the existing oversize outcome.
The help: the self-description and the MCP and command-line help name the new fields of caused and what the cut and the count mean, held in parity across surfaces.

Acceptance on a fixture with a real failure, a panic in a real code path, an Err with a cause chain, a framework or engine record: the test asserts the message, the source location and the cause chain are in the answer, not only that the fields are present.

Acceptance of the scrub: a record with a secret-named field crosses with that field hidden and the rest of its text whole; of the bounds: a message past the cut arrives cut with the cut said, records past the count counted by source.
The acceptance runs in both layout modes and on every surface: in process, through the command line's own binary, and over MCP.
No new verb, carrier, exit code, refusal cause, session error, socket or listener: the existing sets, their order and their counts stay as they are.

The log sink's lines are unchanged: no message, payload or field value reaches a log line, stderr line or span field; the command span and tool_call span keep their fixed fields, the driver log line keeps fixed words and counts, and the text crosses only as the command's answer.
A root-boundary Err fixture runs on its own session, the error the boundary took not leaking into another check's answer.
Committed recorded checks whose kept answers carry caused stay byte-equal to the binary's recording and hold no private data, re-recorded where the answer's shape grows.
Test failures over caused text print no argument value, and a test reading the session host's or MCP child's output finds no screen content or error text on stderr.
